audit_findings.title: The $254.9 million TRA claim is absent from the equity bridge and may not be captured in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $252.390 million filed June 2026 liability; 61.6% of the $410.0 million base equity value and $0.97 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Future TRA payments reduce equity-level OE, or the outstanding liability must be deducted in the equity bridge if those payments are not modeled in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Any payments made to Stagwell Media under the Tax Receivables Agreement will generally reduce the amount of overall cash flow that may have otherwise been available to us.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted claim is demonstrated: the June 2026 balance sheet reports a $252.390 million long-term TRA liability, while the bridge includes no TRA adjustment, and only $2.554 million was paid during the first half of 2026. On a simple bridge-deduction treatment, base equity value would fall from $410.0 million to about $157.6 million, or from $1.58 to about $0.61 per share. The only unresolved issue is whether forecast OE already captures the corresponding payments; the stated method does not establish that it does.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $252.390 million liability to its projected annual payment schedule and forecast cash taxes, then rerun all scenarios either deducting the claim or explicitly reducing OE by the payments without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 attributable numerator may not match the post-exchange Class A denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.637 million filed numerator difference between $29.101 million attributable income and the $22.464 million diluted combined-claim numerator; 31.0% of the $21.4 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The claim basis of the FY2025 OE numerator determines anchor OE, while the post-exchange share count allocates that OE across all current Class A shares.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 4, 2025, Stagwell Media exercised in full its right to exchange all of its 151,648,741 shares of Class C Common Stock, together with the Paired Units in OpCo, for an equal number of newly issued shares of Class A Common Stock.
audit_findings.explanation: A basis mismatch is demonstrated if the $29.101 million parent-attributable amount was used: the filed FY2025 diluted calculation combines that amount with the $6.637 million Class C loss to produce a $22.464 million numerator because the former Class C interests participate in the diluted denominator. The exact OE correction remains unresolved because every cash-flow adjustment must also be allocated on the same claim basis, but the filed numerator difference is large relative to the anchor and could materially lower value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE on a pro-forma all-Class-A basis for the full year, including the pre-exchange Class C allocation, and rerun the valuation using consistently allocated earnings, D&A, capex, working capital, leases and taxes.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-related cash claims and minority puts are missing from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $84.480 million of filed June 2026 recognized claims: $56.867 million deferred acquisition consideration, $20.313 million RNCI and $7.3 million profit-interest liabilities; 20.6% of base equity value, with additional formula-based exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash-settled purchase-price and minority claims reduce the bridge or future OE; stock-settled portions increase diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s obligations extending beyond twelve months primarily consist of deferred acquisition consideration payments, purchases of redeemable noncontrolling interests, subsidiary awards, capital expenditures, scheduled lease obligation payments, and interest payments on borrowings under the Company’s 5.625% Notes (as defined in Note 11 of the Notes included herein) and Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The omissions are demonstrated because the latest filing reports these claims while the bridge contains none of them. Settlement treatment is unresolved: $18.8 million of deferred consideration is expected to be stock-settled, some employment-contingent amounts may already be expensed in OE, and RNCI or profit-interest settlements depend on formulas and exercise conditions. The recognized balances alone are material relative to the $410.0 million base equity value, and maximum exposure may be higher.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 2026 claim schedule separating cash, stock and already-expensed amounts; obtain contractual maximums and exercise dates; deduct unmodeled cash claims, add stock dilution and rerun all scenarios without double counting expenses already retained in OE.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow add-backs may overstate the parent common claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed 2025 components include $29.101 million parent-attributable income, $171.249 million consolidated D&A and $111.230 million consolidated capex plus capitalized software, versus a $21.4 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent NCI allocation changes OE through D&A, capex, capitalized software, leases and working-capital adjustments.
audit_findings.evidence: Stagwell holds a 100% ownership position in substantially all of its Brands, and the remainder are majority owned with management of the Brands owning the remaining equity.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed claim basis is a demonstrated methodological error if parent-attributable income was combined with consolidated cash-flow adjustments. The net direction cannot be established because consolidated positive add-backs can overstate the common claim while consolidated capital spending and working-capital deductions can offset or reverse that effect. The relevant gross components dwarf the anchor, so the unresolved allocation is reasonably capable of changing the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each OE year entirely on a consolidated basis followed by an explicit allocation to NCI and common owners, or entirely on a parent-attributable basis, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The June 2026 bridge and share count include a business absent from FY2025 OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.2 million purchase price, including $4.6 million cash and 863,624 shares valued at $5.6 million, plus up to $24.8 million contingent consideration; gross maximum $35.0 million or 8.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-acquisition cash and shares reduce per-share value while omitted acquired OE increases it; omitted contingent cash or stock consideration works in the opposite direction.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 30, 2026, the Company acquired Wavelength, a digital advocacy and communications company, for an estimated purchase price of $10.2 million, of which approximately $4.6 million was paid in cash and approximately $5.6 million was paid in 863,624 shares of the Company’s Class A Common Stock subject to post-closing adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed scale is insufficient to change the present valuation conclusion. The issued shares are only 0.33% of the 259.139 million denominator, the purchase price is 2.5% of the $410.0 million base value, and even purchase price plus maximum contingent consideration is $35.0 million, or about $0.14 per diluted share before acquired OE. That cannot close the gap between $1.58 base value and the $8.77 market price, although it should be corrected for precision.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Wavelength's pro-forma attributable OE and contingent-settlement mix, then either add it with all consideration and dilution to the June 2026 perimeter or roll cash and shares back to the FY2025 perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Not all reported cash is necessarily excess cash available to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $28.9 million filed June 2026 cash collected and due to receivables purchasers; 26.4% of reported cash, 7.0% of base equity value and about $0.11 per diluted share; additional required operating cash unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Only excess cash belongs in the equity bridge; third-party funds, restricted balances and minimum operating liquidity must be excluded from cash added to equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The trade receivables collected by the Company that were not remitted to the third parties under these arrangements were recorded in Accruals and other liabilities on the Audited Consolidated Balance Sheets and total $21.2 million as of December 31, 2025 and $19.5 million as of December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that $28.9 million was collected but remained payable to third parties, while the valuation adds the entire $109.473 million cash balance. Excluding the known amount alone would reduce base value from about $1.58 to $1.47 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $8.77 price. However, the record does not quantify how much additional cash supports advance billings, accrued media, restrictions or minimum operating liquidity, so total materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace June 2026 bank balances to the $28.9 million remittance liability, restricted funds, advance billings, accrued media and minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.
